 Joel Embiid has been synonymous with a major word throughout his NBA career: injuries. The worry entering the Philadelphia 76ers ' 2026-27 regular-season campaign wasn't that they would fall short. It was also not whether he would mesh well in a lineup with Tyrese Maxey, V.J. Edgecombe, LeBron James, and Jaylen Brown. None of that was a primary concern for Sixers fans. Instead, the concern was that he would have to cut his season short because of another physical issue. That became real during their clash against the Boston Celtics , led by Jayson Tatum.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Embiid has hard, injury-laden fall during 76ers vs. Celtics
 The 76ers were already struggling against the Celtics. They lost the first quarter 30-23, and the second quarter told the same story. As halftime neared, Jayson Tatum had led his squad to 62 points while the 76ers were stuck at 51. But that wasn't the biggest concern for fans inside Xfinity Mobile Arena.
 Joel Embiid was already struggling to find his footing against the Celtics. Before the buzzer sounded to mark halftime, he fell to the ground, and it took a while for his body to regain the strength to rise. Even after that, he was seen limping back to the other side of the court.
 Prior to going down, Embiid had not been able to make a single one of his six field goal attempts despite playing 17 minutes. The 76ers star has tried to make an impact by getting to the free-throw line 11 times and knocking down nine of those shots.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement So far, he has nine points alongside five rebounds. Beyond his inefficiency from the field, the Celtics have also forced him into two turnovers.
 It remains unclear whether the 76ers will err on the side of caution and sideline him for the rest of the game. Regardless, it will affect their chances of getting back in this game to retain their top spot in the Eastern Conference standings.
